blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how plastic bags and nylon clothes are made? They are products of polymers, which are essential in our daily lives.

blocks.markdown: Polymers are large molecules composed of repeated subunits called monomers. These monomers are bonded together in a chain-like fashion. Polymers can be classified into two main types: addition polymers and condensation polymers.

blocks.title: Definition of a Polymer
blocks.text: A polymer is a large molecule made up of repeating structural units called monomers. Examples include polythene and nylon.

blocks.markdown: Addition polymers are formed by the addition reaction of monomers with double bonds, such as ethene forming polythene. Condensation polymers, like nylon, are formed through a condensation reaction where each time a bond is formed, a small molecule like water is released.

blocks.title: Formation of Polythene
blocks.prompt: Explain how polythene is formed from ethene.

steps.text: Ethene molecules, which contain double bonds, undergo an addition reaction.
The double bonds open up and link together, forming long chains of polythene.

blocks.answer: Polythene is formed by the polymerization of ethene through an addition reaction where the double bonds open up and link together.

blocks.markdown: Polythene is widely used in the production of plastic bags, containers, and bottles due to its durability and flexibility. Nylon, on the other hand, is used in making fabrics, ropes, and fishing nets because of its strength and elasticity.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember that addition polymers form without the loss of any small molecules, while condensation polymers form with the release of small molecules like water.

blocks.markdown: Despite their usefulness, plastics pose significant environmental challenges. In Nigeria, plastic waste contributes to pollution, clogging waterways and harming marine life.

points: Polymers are large molecules formed from monomers.
Polythene and nylon are examples of addition and condensation polymers, respectively.
Plastic waste is a significant environmental problem in Nigeria.
